correctness.rationale: The 2a nonzero proper divisor ideals are precisely A_i=(p^i), 1≤i≤a, and B_j=(p^j q), 0≤j<a; each has a nonzero annihilator. Products give no A−A edges and the threshold i+j≥a for A−B or B−B edges (on distinct vertices). From A_1,...,A_{a−1}, the chronological forces A_i→B_{a−i} are legal because B_j with j>a−i are already blue, after which B_1→A_a→B_0 clears the graph. Writing U_i=A_i and V_i=B_{a−i}, the disjoint edges U_iV_i form K_a branch sets since U_jV_i is an edge for i<j. Independently, a width-(a−1) path decomposition consists of the a−1 bags {V_1,...,V_i,U_i,...,U_{a−1}} for 1≤i≤a−1, then {V_1,...,V_{a−1},U_a} and {U_a,V_a}. Vertex occurrences are consecutive; the bags cover U_iV_j iff j≤i and all V−V edges, as V_a has no V-neighbors. The minor lower bound, this path-decomposition upper bound and the forcing/width inequality establish equality; at a=1 the graph is K_2. A fresh finite enumeration from ideal-product divisibility for n=3·2^a, 1≤a≤7, gave Z=1,1,2,3,4,5,6 and minimum-set counts 2,2,6,23,63,207,559. This only corroborates Z for those rings. The packaged verify.py was read but not executed; its recorded finite checks are not the all-exponent proof.
residual_risks: No assertion about a complete classification of minimum forcing sets or a maximum-nullity equality is audited.

evidence: The earlier clique/weak-perfectness calculations supply no K_a minor or optimal forcing sequence. E.g., at a=4 the largest clique has size 3, whereas the four branch sets in the reviewed theorem exhibit a K_4 minor. The general inequality tw≤pw≤Z then converts the two matching bounds into the equality claim.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither colorability, the clique lower bound, independence data nor the general width chain implies the needed graph-specific upper and lower bounds. The first two parameters may also be established by the explicit path decomposition and minor, without relying on the inequality for their upper bounds.

evidence: Resultary 1eca1a8f78f2 treats the identical p^a q family but gives independence data; 7178b3fa1b20 and 86625146ed7a cover compressed and ordinary zero-divisor graphs of individual chain rings, respectively.

For Z/nZ, two elements generate the same principal ideal precisely when their gcd with n coincides, which also determines their annihilator. Thus the annihilator quotient is a meaningful equivalent graph formulation; the single-chain-ring comparisons lack the other prime factor.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing to the compressed graph terminology does not change the arithmetic problem. The retrieved single-chain results and independence polynomial do not establish the claimed parameters for the equivalent two-prime graph.

value.rationale: The exact equality joins a forcing process to a width obstruction in a natural family of ideal-product graphs. The matching explicit sequence, minor and boundary case provide usable sharp test instances of the general inequalities. The value is the structural equality and certificates; merely recovering a from the graph is not new information because its vertex count is 2a.
residual_risks: The parameter formula distinguishes exponents only within the stipulated a≥2 family; a=1 and a=2 both have all three parameters equal to 1.
